mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals a demand contraction with partial offset from residential investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > 2% YoY and HOUST rises > 1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 0.5% MoM for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary tightening and inflationary pressure, which erodes real purchasing power and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth above 0.4% for six consecutive months) signals strengthening household demand, which boosts consumption and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.4% MoM for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the unemployment rate to a historical low below 3.5% while payroll employment growth accelerates signals an overheating labor market, which raises wage inflation and reduces profit margins, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the real retail sales proxy (RSAFS) below -1% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based collapse in consumer demand, which depresses corporate revenues and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls < -1% MoM for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
